name: matrixChain
description: Given matrices A₁, A₂, ..., Aₙ, find the parenthesization minimizing scalar multiplications. Uses DP: dp[i][j] = minimum cost to multiply matrices i through j.
aim: Find the optimal way to parenthesize a chain of matrix multiplications to minimize the total number of scalar multiplications. The order of multiplication affects cost dramatically but not the result.
howItWorks: Let dp[i][j] = min cost to multiply matrices i..j
Base case: dp[i][i] = 0 (single matrix, no multiplication)
For chain length l = 2 to n: try every split point k
dp[i][j] = min over k of: dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + rows[i]*cols[k]*cols[j]
Result: dp[1][n] gives minimum total multiplications

realWorld: Compiler optimization: optimal order for matrix operations in code
Scientific computing: NumPy, BLAS libraries optimize matrix chain order
Machine learning: optimizing tensor contraction order in neural networks
whenToUse: Chained matrix multiplications where matrix dimensions vary
When different parenthesizations have dramatically different costs
alternatives: Greedy: doesn't work here — optimal requires DP
Divide and conquer without memoization: O(4^n) — too slow

beginnerAnalogy: Like deciding the order to multiply numbers in a chain — (2×3)×4 costs 6+8=14 multiplications but 2×(3×4) costs 12+8=20. Matrix chains are the same idea but with bigger numbers.
beginnerWhat: Finding the cheapest order to multiply a sequence of matrices by cleverly splitting the problem.
beginnerWhy: Wrong parenthesization can be 100x more expensive — DP finds optimal order in O(n³).
beginnerWhen: Chained matrix multiplications in scientific computing and machine learning pipelines.
